meta.purpose: How the Scout proves an asset's IDENTITY — that it is what the caption claims. Pick the cheapest sufficient method; set identity.verified=true only on a pass. The validate.py media gate hard-fails a real-subject asset whose identity.verified != true.

steps: Fetch the real page and copy the opaque ID (never from memory).
Call the provider's oEmbed endpoint; require HTTP 200.
Compare the returned title to the claimed label (title sanity check).

trusted_source.for: images / video from Wikidata or Wikimedia Commons
steps: The asset comes from a Wikidata QID property (P18 image / P41 flag / P154 logo) or a Commons file whose description page names the subject.
Record the QID / Commons file + descriptionurl as the proof in identity.verified_title.
trusted_source.note: Commons provenance is strong but not infallible — for the single most load-bearing hero image, also do a vlm_view.

vlm_view.for: any image where identity matters (a named person, a specific place / object)
steps: Open the downloaded file with the Read tool (it renders the image).
Confirm it depicts <subject> AND is a real photo, not an AI render of a real thing.
Record one line of what you actually saw in identity.verified_title.
Record method=vlm_view, verified=true — or, if it does not match, set verified=false and DROP the asset.
Use for ambient / non-specific imagery (a crowd, a pitch) where there is no named subject to confirm.
Set identity.subject='generic', method=manual, verified=true. (License still must be verified.)

frame_verify.for: VIDEO whose depicted EVENT / action matters — a real clip captioned as a specific moment (a goal, a launch, a speech). vlm_view confirms the SUBJECT; frame_verify confirms the EVENT (a clip can show the right person at the WRONG moment).
steps: Extract N sample frames across the clip with ffmpeg (e.g. `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vf fps=1 frame_%03d.png`, or `-ss` at a few timestamps).
Open each frame with the Read tool (vlm_view) and confirm the depicted action/event matches the caption_claims — not just that the subject is present.

On a match, set identity.frame_verified=true with one line of what the frames showed (keep identity.method/verified as the SUBJECT check). If the event does NOT match the claim, set identity.frame_verified=false and DROP or re-caption the clip.
frame_verify.note: frame_verified is recorded ALONGSIDE the subject identity (identity.verified stays the subject check; frame_verified is the event check). validate.py §5 raises media_event_unverified (WARN) for a real-subject video that passed subject-identity but has no identity.frame_verified — a presence nudge, not a hard block; clips that predate the field are grandfathered.

video_clip_quality.resolution_sufficiency: Record the asset's NATIVE pixel size — native_width × native_height — via ffprobe (`ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height -of csv=p=0 FILE`, which reads both video and image dimensions). Do NOT display a low-res clip/image UPSCALED — a 320-wide clip stretched full-bleed looks soft/blurry. Prefer a source whose native width comfortably covers where it will display (a full-bleed / hero asset wants >=1280 wide; a small inline card asset is fine smaller). validate.py §5 raises media_low_resolution (WARN) ONLY when a RECORDED native_width is below the display floor; an unrecorded dimension is skipped (grandfathered).
video_clip_quality.representative_footage: Prefer footage that is REPRESENTATIVE of the moment the caption claims (the actual goal / launch / scene), not a loosely-related stand-in. This is the GOAL, not a penalty — a representative clip strengthens the story; a generic stand-in is acceptable only if honestly captioned as illustrative.

rule: Real-subject media — named people, specific stadiums / landmarks / objects, official logos / flags — MUST be verified by oembed, trusted_source, or vlm_view before any downstream use. For a real-subject VIDEO whose caption claims a specific event, additionally frame_verify the depicted event (record identity.frame_verified). Record native_width/native_height for any displayed clip/image and do not upscale a low-res source. Generic / ambient imagery needs license verification but may use method=manual with subject='generic'.
